Kento Alpha 0.9.48, build 3227

New

  • Kiri's depth defocus works: it softens the foreground to the plate's focus. Match to background (or setting depth defocus the first time) measures how much softer the background's edges are than the foreground's own, and depth defocus puts that share of the blur on the foreground over the plate; the line under it says what it measured. On a test plate blurred by 3 px it measured 2.8.
  • Kiri's General route refines CorridorKey's edge with MEMatte where CorridorKey is unsure, the studio's best recipe for hair (on its tests, the edge's error 0.165 to 0.139, for about a third of a second a frame). It runs when MEMatte's weights are in Kento's models folder; Install doesn't offer them yet.

Changed

  • VectorRetime's Motion is sharper and quicker: its flow is now worked out to about 1,000 pixels across rather than at full size, which on footage with true in-between frames scored better (2K 34.0 to 34.5 dB, 4K 32.4 to 33.4).
  • LightKey's Screen Grow/Shrink grows the matte as NukeX does: level by level, each level's pixels joined. On RAI_150 the windshield key went from 0.052 off NukeX's to 0.0018, the front edge from 0.031 to 0.0047. Half-pixel sizes still differ a little at some corners.
  • Reconcile3D's clamp works as NukeX's: negatives to 0, values over 1 kept.
  • Nuke scripts' menus answer as in Nuke: a menu's items come in its own order and getValue() gives the item's index (VectorRetime's Output Speed had read 2, not 0), and menus made from Gaffer's preset lists are found. Kento's own Python API (kento) now sits under the nuke module, and render nodes have it too.
  • Nagi's learned method: the tooltip and manual now say to keep non-local means for grainy plates. On fine film grain it takes out about twice as much as learned; learned is the cleanest on even sensor noise.

Fixed

  • Gaffer's hash cache is capped at about a tenth of the machine's memory: on a deep comp it could hold some 4 million entries on every thread, about 20 GB on a 16-core Mac (MC1_050's frozen Kento); now about 7 GB at most there. Comps render as fast as before; MC1_050's slowest nodes are still slow where Gaffer works them out.

Kento Alpha 0.9.47, build 3200

New

  • Nagi has a learned denoiser: its spatial method's third choice, learned, runs OpenImageDenoise's neural denoiser on the graphics card after Nagi's temporal stage, with spatial luma and chroma setting how much of its change is kept. On a test frame it took the noise from 0.040 to 0.008, against 0.013 for non-local means. It can smooth fine texture, so watch skin and fabric. A Nuke script saves it as non-local means.
  • Kiri at 4K works on the subject, not the whole frame: with a garbage matte from the matte input (Click the subject, a Roto) and tiles off, the General route keys the box round the subject over the shot, at full detail when it fits, and puts the matte back in place. On 10 of 13 test shots it matched or beat fitting the whole frame, at the same cost. The cost line says when it's used.
  • The Lens node's Work it out solves a degree-6 or fisheye model's own terms from the grid, so a model change fits the chart itself rather than a conversion of another model's numbers.
  • CameraTracker uses a Known Lens: the tracks go through the lens before the solve. It has a Lens section (lens type, distortion, quartic, center) and an Undistort output that grows to fit, as NukeX's does. Saved to a Nuke script, a Known Lens is written as Unknown Lens, which NukeX opens.
  • Drop a comp on the Node Graph with Option held and its nodes are added to this comp where you dropped them, instead of opening it.

Changed

  • A busy node's input names (three or more on one side, as Kiri has), when you point at it, form a staircase: each top input's name just right of its own wire, a line above the next, with the wires passing behind the words. No name lands on another, or on the node's name, at any zoom; they had run together ("degrained matte").
  • Copy and paste between Kento and NukeX checked both ways with NukeX itself.
  • VectorRetime's blend if unsure measured against true in-between frames: it scored about 3 dB below plain Motion on every test clip, so the manual now says to leave it off unless a retime tears.
  • The updater picks its own system's builds from the feed, ready for the Windows build.

Kento Alpha 0.9.46, build 3173

New

  • Kiri matches the plate's grain: turn on match the plate's grain (Balance) and the background's grain is put on the foreground, inside its matte, at the foreground's brightness, so a clean subject sits in a grainy plate. Key from the degrained copy for it, so the foreground's own grain comes out first.
  • Kiri draws its edge band: change the band's width and the band shows over the picture in yellow for a moment, round the matte's edge, with its width named and the place you picked the screen ringed. Pick screen now remembers where it sampled.
  • FilmLab has halation and grain, as Asobi's Film Lab does: a halation box with strength, size, threshold, hue, bounce and scatter, working on the scene light before the look, and a grain box with amount, color and seed. A look's settings keep its halation.
  • FilmLab's negative and print menus show headings: motion picture, still, black-and-white and reversal negatives; motion picture prints, photographic paper, black-and-white and reversal prints.

Changed

  • The Color menu is in submenus: Grade and correct, Looks and film, Color spaces, OCIO, Math and 3D LUT. The toolbar's Grade button is gone: ReviewGrade, CDLLook, Look and FilmLab are under Color > Looks and film. A favourite whose node moved is still found.
  • The Lens node asks before a model change it can't fit closely: it says how far off the closest fit would be and why (NukeX Classic's anamorphic terms, for one), with Change anyway (one undo) or keep the model you had. It had switched back without a word.
  • While the Assistant answers, it says how long it's been, with a Stop button in words beside it.
  • A clone's time offset in a Nuke script renders as NukeX renders it: it works when the clone's source is a background input and does nothing on the foreground, as in NukeX. Clones painted in Kento keep their time offset on any source.
  • Renders use memory better: deep pictures (ScanlineRender's cards) and the 4K planes a comp keeps asking for are reused from frame to frame instead of taken fresh each time.

Fixed

  • The Assistant through Claude Code no longer hangs when it adds nodes: its Apply and Skip card failed to appear, and the reply waited for ever.
  • Settings > AI and MCP: the assistant menu takes another app; it had stayed on the first.
  • A pane's Split Vertical and Split Horizontal give two even halves; the new pane had come out a sliver, squeezing the panels beside it. The pane menu says Close Pane (it showed "emove Panel").
  • The icons in a pane's corner stay put: hovering over them brought back blank squares. The editor focus button shows what the pane follows (the selection, the Focus Node, a bookmark, or pinned).
